scope: Proposition 33.5 (Global static classification) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 218. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The positive component is the whole original open exterior: U = int Ω and N > 0 there. Its attached boundary is S. There is a global isometry of the static base onto the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spatial exterior of mass m, under which (33.26) hb =  1 + m 2ρ2 2 ( dρ2 + ρ2 gS3 ), λ = 1 − m/(2ρ2) 1 + m/(2ρ2) , ρ ≥ q m/2. The isometry is smooth on the open base and in its one-sided regular boundary structure. The attachment is homeomorphic to the original attachment of S in Ω and restricts smoothly on S. In particular the open base is simply connected and S is a round three-sphere in its induced metric. The base reflection is smooth in signed λ in the positive boundary-lapse case; its angular coordinates can be taken constant along base normal geodesics.
